title: The Jacobians block of a buffer-stock results file (DRAFT, not yet part of results.schema.json)
description: DRAFT of 2026-11-01, on the design approved at 17:05:24 EST (../jacobians.md). It validates the optional top-level key `jacobians` of a results file of the buffer-stock families. It is not referenced by results.schema.json until the owner approves it.

T.description: The horizon, in periods: every matrix is T x T.

inputs.description: The inputs, each a column index s of every matrix: the date at which its perturbed value applies.

outputs.description: The outputs, each a row index t: C consumption, A end-of-period assets before that period's deaths, Y_hh the households' non-capital income, transfers included.

conventions.description: The conventions no matrix shows, stated so that the checker and a reader can verify them.

dating.description: For each input, in words, the date its value applies and to what; for example, for return: 'the gross return paid at the start of s on assets carried from s - 1'.

units.const: per capita, per unit of the steady state's aggregate permanent income

measure.description: The measure the distribution is pushed forward under.

assets.description: A newborn's assets, in units of its permanent income.

first_period.description: In words, what a newborn draws in its first period, for example 'the employed branch of xi, psi drawn'.

grid.description: The shared distribution grid on end-of-period assets: a_j = a_max ((x x) x) with x = j/(N - 1), in IEEE double precision.

nodes_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the N nodes as little-endian float64, in order.

mass_above_a_max.description: Per type and in aggregate, the mass whose end-of-period assets exceed a_max, which the lottery puts at a_max.

clipped_output_mass.description: For a toolkit that bins an output on a grid of its own, the mass clipped at that grid's ends, per output.

step.description: The finite difference's step, in the input's units; absent for automatic differentiation.

baseline.description: What the perturbed path is differenced against.

steady_state.description: The steady state the Jacobians linearize around.

tolerance.description: The steady-state solve's stopping tolerance; the suite requires 1e-10 or tighter.

backward_step_residual.description: The largest change in the policy from one backward step at the steady state.

weights.description: Each type's weight in the aggregate: its share of aggregate permanent income, in the order of the parameter file's types.

matrices.description: One entry per output, input and type, and per output and input for the aggregate.

type.description: The 0-based index of the type, or 'aggregate'.

ingredients.description: Optional: the fake-news ingredients on the toolkit's own grid of K nodes, from which a harness rebuilds the matrices.

transition.description: The steady-state transition, K x K, as COO triplets: row i the node the mass leaves, rows summing to one, next period's distribution D Lambda.

distribution.description: The steady-state distribution, K, as a .npy file.

output_values.description: Each output's values at the K nodes.

news.description: For each input and type: the first-period responses of each output, dY0 (T), and of the distribution, dD1 (T x K).

RelativePath.description: A path relative to the results file, to a .npy file: version 1.0, little-endian float64 (int64 for indices), C order.

Coo.description: A sparse array as three .npy files: 0-based int64 rows and columns and float64 values, in row-major order, sorted, with no pair repeated and no explicit zero.

rho.description: R times survival: the factor that turns this period's A into next period's resources.

mpc_mean_income.description: The mean MPC under the income measure, which J^{C,transfer}[0,0] equals.
